summary: The result contains one value for every tree node, imposing an Omega(n) output-size lower bound. The iterative preorder traversal visits each node once and matches that bound.

optimality.argument: A correct preorder result for an n-node tree has exactly n entries, including duplicates at distinct nodes, so merely producing the output requires Omega(n) work. The current stack traversal pushes, pops, and appends each node exactly once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every node contributes one position to the returned preorder sequence, so no node can be omitted from output construction.
Each node is pushed by its parent at most once, popped once, and appended once.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover sparse and branching trees, an empty tree, and a singleton; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
